stem: A 34-year-old man passes large volumes of dilute urine after a basal skull fracture. Serum sodium is high, and urine concentrates after an injection of desmopressin. The hormone he lacks is stored in a pituitary lobe and made by hypothalamic neurons.
oneliner: 34M + basal skull fracture + polyuria, dilute urine, high Na + concentrates with desmopressin → which origin of the lobe storing the lost hormone?
ask: The lobe that stores the missing hormone arises from which embryonic tissue?

whyNot.A: That is the **anterior pituitary**, which makes its own hormones
whyNot.C: Gives **adrenal medulla and melanocytes**, not the lobe holding hypothalamic terminals
whyNot.D: Gives gut lining and **thyroid**-region derivatives, not pituitary tissue
whyNot.E: Gives the **thymus and inferior parathyroids**, not a pituitary lobe

why: Dilute urine that **responds to desmopressin** is central diabetes insipidus from lost ADH. ADH is made in the hypothalamus and stored in the **posterior pituitary**, which grows down from the **neuroectoderm** of the diencephalon, unlike the anterior lobe from **Rathke pouch**.

idea.rule: Posterior pituitary is neuroectoderm; anterior pituitary is oral ectoderm of Rathke pouch.
also: Posterior lobe holds axon terminals and pituicytes, not hormone-making cells
The pituitary stalk (infundibulum) is also neuroectoderm
Craniopharyngioma arises from Rathke pouch (oral ectoderm) remnants
Anterior lobe (oral ectoderm) makes ACTH, TSH, GH, prolactin, FSH and LH

stem: A 16-year-old girl is short and has primary amenorrhea with no breast development. FSH is high and the karyotype is 45,X. Pelvic ultrasound shows a small uterus and cervix with streak gonads.
oneliner: 16F + short + primary amenorrhea + no breast development + high FSH + 45,X + small uterus, streak gonads → uterus comes from which structure?
ask: Her uterus develops from which embryonic structure?

whyNot.A: Form **male ducts** (epididymis, vas deferens) and need **testosterone**, absent with streak gonads
whyNot.B: Forms the **lower vagina**, bladder and urethra, not the uterus and cervix seen on her ultrasound
whyNot.D: Forms the **clitoris** of the external genitalia, not an internal organ
whyNot.E: Forms the **gonads** themselves, here the **streak gonads**, not the uterus

answer: Paramesonephric (Mullerian) ducts, which persist by default
why: With no Y chromosome there are no **Sertoli cells**, so no **anti-Mullerian hormone** is made. The **paramesonephric ducts** then form the uterus, tubes, cervix and upper vagina **by default**, even with **streak gonads**; the uterus is small because she lacks estrogen.

idea.rule: Uterus, tubes and upper vagina come from paramesonephric ducts, which persist unless anti-Mullerian hormone removes them.
also: Androgen insensitivity (46,XY) has no uterus because Sertoli cells make AMH
Mullerian agenesis (MRKH) gives absent uterus with normal ovaries and breasts
Fusion failure of the paramesonephric ducts gives bicornuate uterus

stem: A 45-year-old woman who sings professionally has weakness of one cricothyroid muscle after a thyroidectomy and can no longer raise her pitch. Her vocal cords move normally and she is not hoarse.
oneliner: 45F + singer + after thyroid surgery cannot raise pitch + cricothyroid weakness + cords move normally → which pharyngeal arch?
ask: The injured nerve belongs to which pharyngeal arch?

whyNot.A: The 1st arch nerve is the **mandibular division of the trigeminal**, supplying the muscles of mastication, not the larynx
whyNot.B: The 2nd arch nerve is the **facial nerve**, supplying the muscles of facial expression
whyNot.C: The 3rd arch nerve is the **glossopharyngeal**, supplying only the stylopharyngeus
whyNot.E: The 6th arch nerve is the **recurrent laryngeal**, which moves the other laryngeal muscles; her **cords move normally** and she is **not hoarse**

answer: 4th pharyngeal arch (superior laryngeal nerve, from the vagus)
why: The cricothyroid is supplied by the **superior laryngeal nerve**, the nerve of the **4th pharyngeal arch**. The other intrinsic laryngeal muscles are supplied by the **recurrent laryngeal nerve of the 6th arch**, which is why her cords move normally and she is not hoarse.

idea.rule: 4th arch = superior laryngeal nerve (cricothyroid, pharyngeal constrictors, levator veli palatini); 6th arch = recurrent laryngeal nerve (other intrinsic laryngeal muscles).
also: Both laryngeal nerves are branches of the vagus nerve
The right recurrent nerve hooks under the right subclavian (4th arch artery); the left hooks under the ligamentum arteriosum (6th arch)
The 6th arch artery forms the pulmonary arteries and the ductus arteriosus
The 4th arch artery forms the aortic arch on the left and the proximal right subclavian on the right
